guard: a handler that owns external state repairs it on takeover without being wired to
why: Found by review, and the finding was not that the seam was wrong -- it was that the seam had NO
CALLER. `onActivated` was optional and nothing in the tree passed one, not a production path and
not this suite, so every adopted run left its checkpoint timers armed at the predecessor's
instance and epoch, firing onto subjects nobody consumes. Replaying the program does not repair
that: the pause replays as pending and goes straight back to waiting.
An optional hook with no caller is INDISTINGUISHABLE AT RUNTIME from a driver that has nothing
to repair, which is why no test caught it and why the repair is a default rather than a note. A
handler that knows how to repair its own state declares `adopted`; the driver still only decides
WHEN, which was the original design and stays intact.
Two of the four mutations are narrowness. A default that OVERRODE an explicit callback, or that
required every handler to carry the method, would satisfy the headline cell perfectly -- and one
of those turns the callback into dead surface while the other refuses every handler in this file
that owns no external state at all.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY, and it is one config away rather than absent. Every mutation config in
this lane mutates a module its suite imports through a RELATIVE `../src/*.js` path, and no
command carries a build step -- all are bare `tsx` -- so the mutated bytes are the bytes the
suite loads. The suites in THIS directory nonetheless boot `@cotal-ai/core` and `@cotal-ai/lang`
through package specifiers that resolve to `dist`. So a future config that targets
`packages/lang/src` or `packages/core/src` under a `pnpm smoke:runtime-*` command would be VOID
ON ARRIVAL: the mutant would sit in `src` while the suite graded an untouched `dist`, and the
kill rate would measure module resolution rather than the guard. Either mutate the module the
suite imports relatively, or put a build between the mutation and the run.

mutations.name: the default is removed: the seam goes back to a hook nothing passes
mutations.expectRed: REPAIRED: a successor repairs the previous holder's state WITHOUT any callback being wired
mutations.cell: REPAIRED: a successor repairs the previous holder's state WITHOUT any callback being wired
mutations.note: This is the shipped state before the repair. It passed every test in the tree, which is the whole reason the finding needed a reviewer rather than a suite.

mutations.name: PARANOID: the handler's method OVERRIDES an explicit callback instead of backing it
mutations.expectRed: an explicit onActivated still wins: the default is a fallback, not a replacement
mutations.cell: an explicit onActivated still wins: the default is a fallback, not a replacement
mutations.note: The precedence is the difference between a default and a hijack. A caller that passes a callback has stated what the repair is; taking the handler's instead would silently ignore an explicit instruction, and the headline cell cannot see it because both orders call SOMETHING.

mutations.name: the repair is called, but handed nothing to repair
mutations.expectRed: ...and is handed the prefix the activation validated, which is what names the pauses to re-arm
mutations.cell: ...and is handed the prefix the activation validated, which is what names the pauses to re-arm
mutations.note: A repair handed nothing cannot re-arm anything, so `it was called` is not the property. Note this passes the FRESH-run cell, whose prefix is legitimately empty -- which is why that cell is a control and not the proof.

mutations.name: PARANOID: every handler is assumed to carry the method
mutations.expectRed: and a handler that owns no external state needs no method: the takeover still completes
mutations.cell: and a handler that owns no external state needs no method: the takeover still completes
mutations.note: The other narrowness twin. Every other cell in this file drives a handler that owns nothing external, so a driver that demanded the method would break the ordinary case while the takeover cells above stayed green.
